Specs run in a bubblewrap jail on Linux
units.problem: On macOS every spec runs in a `sandbox-exec` jail that denies each write outside the checkout's `.cache` and the run's temp folder. On Linux, which is CI and any developer's Linux box, specs run **unjailed**, guarded by environment fences only (`scripts/lib/fence.sh`: git ceiling, ref and push hooks, no network transport for git). `@tests/lib/fixture` checks where a command starts, not what it does (R0021 review 001 F4): `fixture.exec(fx, "sh", {"-c", "cd <real checkout> && git checkout -- ."})`...
units.solution: `tests/lib/fence.luau` gets a Linux branch in `jail()`: the specs run under `bwrap` with the whole filesystem read-only, `/run` hidden (the host's sockets there) and `/tmp` private, the checkout's `.cache` and the run's temp folder writable, a private `/dev` and `/proc`, and private pid, network and IPC namespaces in a session of their own that die with the run. The launcher records itself in the run's lock. `PICKMAN_TEST_JAIL` says `bwrap`. A host where it cannot start goes through the same "ou...

design.heading: Design
design.text:
Chore. No change for players: nothing under `pickman/src/` or `pickman/tests/` is touched. Not `solo`; `size: 1400` (the lesson files the merge pass writes, about 100 of them at 10 to 15 lines, the sentences that sharpen existing ones, three documents, one pattern in `lessons.luau`; the ledgers are `.tracker` documents and the specs are prep's, neither counted). The estimate is soft (E4): 13 drafts came from 24 old findings, 1 from 11 already-harvested entries, and the merge pass decides how many survive.

**Facts on `main` at e0b266e7 (2026-11-01), measured with c0136's prototype applied** (`./zn lessons` on a throwaway clone, E1): 157 lessons; 92 item folders hold 1937 findings in design, code and stream reviews (stream: 19 files, 40 findings); 1011 review entries and 60 notes (1071 harvest lines) name no step; 926 findings (886 design and code, 40 stream) have no line at all, in 39 items; 35 batches of at most 150 KB of review and refute text hold all of it (5.8 MB; E3). About 48 of the 1011 entries name lessons of two skills or more, 4 of them of three.

units.problem:
tests/run's jail sweeper was killed with signal 9 during the full gate of tracker.sh done R0035 (2026-10-22), on a machine running several other worktrees' suites; no process of the run was left and the repository was unchanged; the retry passed. Find what sends the SIGKILL (a spec signalling a reused pid in its own sandbox, or the OS under memory pressure) and make the runner tell the two apart.

**Second occurrence (2026-10-26).** `z-nile/check.sh --full` in `.worktree/prep-finished-claude-sca...
units.solution: When the sweeper dies of a signal, the launcher (`fence.REAPER`) looks before it stops the specs' group and prints a second line after the existing one: when, how many seconds after the specs started, its own pid, the run's top process and whether it lives, the memory the OS saw (percent free and swap used), the specs' group (the sweeper's own pid), whether the watchdog lives, every other process still in the group with its command line, and its reading of them in words. design.heading: What prep found
design.text:
- **No spec can reach the sweeper by pid.** The sweeper (`perl -e SWEEPER -`) is the jail's first process, started before every spec, and lives until the run ends, so no pid a spec records (its own children, or a dead one reused) can be the sweeper's. Every `kill -KILL <pid>` in z-nile's specs (c0076, c0078, c0079, `fence-leftovers`, `sweeper-interlock`) names a process the spec started, and every nested sweep is narrowed by `PICKMAN_SWEEP_ONLY` to pids the case lists.
- **What could reach it from inside:** only a group signal. The specs' group is the sweeper's (the launcher's child calls `setpgrp(0, 0)`, forks the watchdog, and then `exec`s `sandbox-exec … perl -e SWEEPER`), and every spec worker is in it unless it moves, so a `kill 0` (or `kill -KILL 0`, or perl's `kill 'KILL', -getpgrp()`) from any spec process in that group kills the sweeper and every spec at once. It can't kill the watchdog: the watchdog was forked before `sandbox-exec`, so it is outside the jail, and the jail's rule refuses a spec's signal to it (the profile's own comment says so). A group signal from outside the jail does kill it. No spec sends a group signal today: the nested launchers and watchdogs (c0076, c0077, c0079 specs) signal their own new groups.
